name: MAmmoTH2
abstract: MAmmoTH2 shows that the web already contains the instruction data everyone pays to create: it harvests roughly ten million naturally occurring instruction–response pairs from pretraining corpora, then refines them — lifting reasoning benchmarks dramatically without human annotation or frontier-model distillation.
contributions: A three-stage pipeline — recall candidate documents, extract Q&A pairs, refine them — yields the ~10M-example WebInstruct corpus from the open web.
Requires neither crowdworkers nor distillation from proprietary models, changing the cost structure of instruction data.
Tuning on WebInstruct lifts base models sharply on reasoning suites, and MAmmoTH2-Plus variants remain competitive instruction models at their scale.
method: Recall finds instruction-shaped documents in web corpora; extraction isolates the Q&A; refinement cleans and completes the pairs.
The paper reports large math-reasoning gains for tuned models against their own baselines.
Follows MAmmoTH, whose MathInstruct corpus hybridized chain-of-thought and program-of-thought rationales.
